newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech July CPI quickens to highest level in year.
newsitem.headline: Czech July CPI quickens to highest level in year.

text.p: Czech consumer inflation, as expected, jumped sharply in July, pushed higher by several price deregulations to reach its highest level year-on-year since August 1996.

The Czech Statistical Bureau (CSU) released CPI data on Friday showing month-on-month inflation for July was 3.5 percent -- the biggest rise since 1993 -- putting the year-on-year rate at 9.4 percent.
A Reuter survey of analysts on Thursday had predicted an increase in prices of 2.4 percent on average, but estimates among the nine experts canvassed ranged from 1.7 percent to 3.8 percent.
Since December, the year-on-year rate steadily dropped from 8.6 percent to a record low of 6.3 percent in May, but in June the trend reversed as the year-on-year rate rose to 6.8 percent.
July's year-on-year rate is the highest since August 1996, when inflation reached 9.6 percent.

The CSU said liberalisation of rents and energy prices was at the heart of the increase, accounting for 3.252 percent points of the month-on-month figure. Core inflation for July was 0.366 percent, the bureau said.

Housing prices rose 18.9 percent, month-on-month, on the heels of a 50 percent rise in rents for state housing on July 1. Prices in the leisure sector also jumped markedly, rising 5.9 percent, month-on-month.
The CSU said prices have risen 31.0 percent from the average level for 1994 while the sliding average in July using a 1993 base was 7.9 percent.
At the end of June, the CSU changed its average 1997 inflation forecast to between 8.5 and 9.5 percent from 8.2 to 8.8 percent.
The Czech crown was little changed on the release of the data. Dealers said a liquidity shortage and market expectations of higher inflation were keeping the currency steady.
The crown was trading at 18.478 to the mark just after the figures were published from 18.486 before the announcement, while the crown/dollar was trading at 34.495 after 34.474 before the data.
